title: Two British men charged with helping Iran over Fairford airbase incident | CNN
text:
British prosecutors said on Tuesday they had charged two British nationals under the National Security Act over an incident last month at the RAF Fairford airbase, with police saying the two were suspected of assisting Iran.

RAF Fairford had been used by US B-1 bombers to carry out strikes on Iran, but they were withdrawn on security grounds shortly after five men were arrested outside the military base in southwest England in the early hours of September 27.

The Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) said Tuesday it had charged Mohmed Abdulkarim, 24, with engaging in conduct that was likely to materially assist a foreign intelligence service.

Nouman Essghir, 24, was charged with one offense of entering a prohibited place for a purpose prejudicial to the UK on August 22. The pair, who both live in London, will appear at Westminster Magistrate’s Court later on Tuesday.

Five other men arrested in connection with the case remain on police bail.

Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor, head of national counter terrorism policing in the UK, said police believed the country Abdulkarim was assisting was Iran.

“We have seen a range of incidents in recent months that we believe have been directed by the Iranian state, and as the director general of Mi5 (the UK’s domestic security service) said just the other week, we are working together to intervene, identify and respond to that threat,” Taylor added.

Initially the police arrested five men “on suspicion of preparation of a terrorist act” and explosives offenses near the Fairford airbase that has long used by the US Air Force. The men were then released on bail, which Taylor on Tuesday acknowledged “sparked significant questions and speculation about the investigation and why that was the case.”

“We know that decisions made during our investigations can sometimes appear illogical to those on the outside, but I want to make it very clear, that there will always be good reason, or rationale behind them,” he added. “Like our adversaries, our tactics vary – and may not always be obvious.”

Taylor said the decision to initially release the men “led to swifter progress, better evidence and ultimately us securing the charges.”

Earlier this month, British Prime Minister Andy Burnham said that the suspected plot targeting RAF Fairford was “almost certainly directed by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard.” Iran has firmly rejected the accusations.

US President Donald Trump praised the arrest of the men at the time, telling reporters that the US had worked with Britain and that the men arrested were planning to do “big damage” to RAF Fairford.

“We had them under view for a long time, and we got them,” Trump said. US intelligence had tracked planning by Iranian groups to target US assets at the base weeks ahead of any arrests, according to multiple sources familiar with the matter.

Days after the initial arrests, the USmoved all of its long-range bombers from RAF Fairfordfollowing an unspecified threat, a knowledgeable source said.

At the time, Trump and Vice President JD Vance hinted that a threat against US assets had prompted the move.

“I think we can say that — I mean, they didn’t fly out by accident,” Trump said. “There were some threats, and rather than tempting the enemy, we’ll capture the enemy and beat the enemy. But why should we leave them there? So we moved them around a little bit.”

Vance said the move was made “out of an abundance of caution,” suggesting it was a response to a potential threat from Iran even as he declined to detail the specific concerns.

CNN’s Billy Stockwell contributed to this report.

CNN’s Billy Stockwell contributed to this report.
